mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a steady four-week improvement from -28.1 to -7.1 percent, indicating a self-reinforcing recovery momentum in discretionary mobility that should continue pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose each of the last 4 weeks from -28.1 to -7.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite the prior four-week monotonic uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: Once TRANSIT mobility crosses above the -10 percent-change threshold, it signals that commuting and errand-linked trips have substantially normalized, which mechanically increases incidental retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -10% change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -8.1 at t-0w, just above the -10 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the subsequent two weeks even though TRANSIT remains above -10 percent change from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A joint pattern of WORKPLACES recovering toward baseline while RESIDENTIAL declines toward zero indicates households are simultaneously resuming office routines and reducing home-bound behavior, and only when both shift together does discretionary retail mobility rise meaningfully over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -41.4 to -17.1 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.6 to -0.1 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even when WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL move in the hypothesized opposite directions concurrently for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The unusually elevated PARKS mobility (62.4 percent above baseline) reflects a transient late-summer/early-autumn outdoor activity peak that generates incidental nearby retail visits; as seasonal cooling sets in over the coming weeks this parks-driven halo effect will fade, slowing or reversing RETAIL_REC gains.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to 62.4 at t-0w, the highest of the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 28 days even as PARKS mobility declines from its current elevated level.

mechanism_narrative: Continued strong week-on-week increases in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -5.6 to 13.0 percent) suggest households are substituting discretionary retail trips with grocery and pharmacy errands, which should dampen or flatten RETAIL_REC growth within the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose roughly 4-10 points weekly over the snapshot period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM increase exceeding 3 points, contradicting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -15 percent change from baseline, it signals that office-return policies have reached a critical mass of enforcement or voluntary compliance, which should boost weekday retail and recreation footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -15% change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -17.1 at t-0w, approaching the -15 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of WORKPLACES crossing above -15 percent change from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of sustained post-pandemic policy normalization, the simultaneous narrowing of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT deficits from baseline reflects institutional relaxation of restrictions, which should continue driving RETAIL_REC upward over a full four-week horizon as long as no new restriction policy is reintroduced.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT deficits narrowed consistently over the four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days despite continued narrowing of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT deficits, absent any new restriction announcement.

mechanism_narrative: The combined acceleration of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recovery indicates a synergistic effect where commuting infrastructure usage and office attendance jointly amplify retail foot traffic near transit hubs and business districts, producing a stronger RETAIL_REC rise over two weeks than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise more than 5 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 8 points and WORKPLACES rose 2.2 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks is no greater than growth observed when only one of TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises sharply, rejecting the synergistic interaction claim.
